transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Dana Liu (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Luma Security), Carlos Ortega (Luma CTO), Priya Singh (Luma DevOps), Alex Novak (Luma Product)

Auto-generated summary: Luma wants to understand Redwood's security posture for hosting sensitive customer PII and regulated datasets; primary decision factors are compliance artifacts, SSO integration, ability to use customer-managed keys, and audit log retention for SOC/PCI audits.

00:00 Dana Liu: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm dana from redwood, i'm joined by ravi our se, uh quick quick agenda — security posture, compliance artifacts, integration concerns, and next steps. sound good?
00:18 Maya Chen: yep that's perfect, thanks dana. we handle a lot of personal health identifiers and some regulated finance stuff for clients so we need to make sure whatever we run meets our compliance.
00:28 Carlos Ortega: and timeline wise we want to decide between hosted vs dedicated by the end of q2, so about three months.
00:37 Ravi Patel: great, that fits a typical eval. quick q on current stack — what are you using for idp? sso?
00:44 Priya Singh: we use okta for SSO, SAML, and SCIM for provisioning. also we have a central kms in gcp — cloud kms — for other services.
00:53 Ravi Patel: ok good. redwood supports SAML/OIDC via okta, scim for user provisioning. for hosted customers we offer SSO + scim and role based access controls that map to groups. for dedicated/private you get the same controls but you can also bring network isolation.
01:12 Maya Chen: do you have SOC 2 docs and an iso cert? we need type II and iso 27001 evidence ideally.
01:20 Dana Liu: yes we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. i'll share the reports under NDA — ravi will attach the SOC2 and our iso artifact.
01:29 Alex Novak: is SOC 2 up to date? date range?
01:33 Dana Liu: our most recent SOC2 Type II covers 2025-07 through 2026-01 — we'll send the report and control matrix.
01:39 Maya Chen: good. questions on encryption — we need keys to be under our control if possible, or at least an HSM/BYOK option. what do you offer?
01:48 Ravi Patel: for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via KMS integrations — we call it BYOK where the customer manages key material in their cloud KMS and we reference it. for private deployments you can run your own HSM. the hosted path uses our KMS wrapper but supports external keys in GCP/AWS/Azure.
02:07 Carlos Ortega: so you support BYOK for hosted? any additional attestation?
02:11 Ravi Patel: yes BYOK supported. there is a short onboarding to set up kms roles and grant encrypt/decrypt to the service principal. we can provide the IAM templates.
02:20 Priya Singh: we need to confirm whether keys ever leave our control ring — are there any copies or exports?
02:25 Ravi Patel: no exported plaintext. keys are used via the cloud kms API, we don't store plaintext keys. i'll include the security brief on key management.
02:33 Maya Chen: also audit logs — for compliance we need immutable audit logs for admin actions and data access. how long do you retain logs and can we pull them into our SIEM?
02:44 Dana Liu: by default hosted retains audit logs 90 days, but enterprise customers can extend retention and we can stream logs to your SIEM (splunk/elastic/chronicle). for dedicated/private you get longer retention and direct log streaming.
02:57 Carlos Ortega: what format are the logs? syslog? json? we want structured events with user id, action, resource, timestamp and request ids for traceability.
03:07 Ravi Patel: logs are JSON structured events with request_id, user, role, action, resource, latency, and model metadata. we support event export via Kafka, syslog, or pushing to cloud storage.
03:20 Maya Chen: do you provide an append-only tamper-evident store or at least signed logs?
03:25 Ravi Patel: we don't re-implement a block-chain but we do provide WORM-like storage for archived logs and maintain checksums; we can also integrate with customers' archival buckets with object locks for immutability.
03:36 Alex Novak: ok on RBAC. we have internal teams and want to ensure we can map Okta groups to roles and have per-team model access — can we do per-route permissions?
03:45 Ravi Patel: yes, RBAC maps Okta groups to roles in the console and you can apply policies per model or per API key. for dedicated/private you can enforce tenant isolation at the network and runtime level.
03:57 Priya Singh: one of our big concerns is data residency — some customers require EU-only hosting and long retention. do you offer region isolation for hosted?
04:06 Dana Liu: yes we have region controls for hosted regions in eu-west and us-east; we can pin workloads to region. for stricter requirements dedicated in-region or private deployment is recommended.
04:18 Carlos Ortega: on the private deployment — what's required for on-prem? do you manage it or do we?
04:22 Ravi Patel: private options range — we have a customer-managed deployment package where you host the runtime in your VPC/on-prem and we provide the control plane guidance; alternatively there is a Redwood-managed private offering where we operate it in your network under contract.
04:36 Maya Chen: for audit purposes we need proof of separation of duties and change control logs for config changes, can you surface that?
04:42 Dana Liu: we can expose change audit trails for deployments, config changes, and role grants. those are included with enterprise packages and can be exported to your audit systems.
04:54 Alex Novak: any third-party pen tests?
04:57 Ravi Patel: we run annual pen tests and share summaries; full reports are available under NDA.
05:04 Priya Singh: SLA questions — if we go dedicated what's the latency and uptime guarantees? we have 99.9% requirement for latency-sensitive flows.
05:12 Dana Liu: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and predictable throughput; for latency we offer configs tuned for lower p99s, and we can provide benchmarks for your workload. we'll run a short benchmark as part of the pilot.
05:25 Carlos Ortega: talk to me about model fallbacks and sensitive data handling — we plan to send customer PII for enrichment in some flows; we need guarantee models won't be logged or used for training.
05:36 Ravi Patel: Redwood does not use customer request data for training. requests can be marked no-retain and there's a data handling policy. for sensitive flows we recommend dedicated/private so there's stricter isolation and you can opt out of any logging of payloads.
05:50 Maya Chen: retention policy — how long do you keep request payloads and embeddings by default? we need defaults and the option to shorten to 0 days for certain datasets.
05:59 Dana Liu: default request logs and payloads for hosted are retained 30 days for troubleshooting, embeddings retention is 90 days; enterprise customers can request shorter windows and some regulated deployments can set retention to 0 for PII. we'll document the options.
06:14 Alex Novak: ok cool. networking specifics — VPC peering vs private link? which do you support?
06:20 Ravi Patel: we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and direct peering options, plus on-prem connectors for air-gapped. we'll share network diagrams and firewall rules required.
06:29 Priya Singh: for onboarding what's the sequence? do we start with hosted for dev and then move to dedicated?
06:34 Dana Liu: common path is start hosted (quick), run a pilot to validate latency and correctness, then move to dedicated reserved capacity for prod, or private if you need on-prem/regulatory controls.
06:44 Carlos Ortega: any gotchas for tokenization or data masking? we do masking at app layer but want advice on best practices.
06:50 Ravi Patel: we recommend client-side tokenization or pre-processing with deterministic hashing for PII, plus request-level flags to avoid storing payloads. we can share a best-practices doc.
06:59 Maya Chen: ok we also need to know about identity federation — can we auto-provision users from Okta into the console and enforce SCIM groups?
07:05 Dana Liu: yes SCIM provisioning supported; group mapping for roles is configurable.
07:10 Alex Novak: can we see a sample audit log event?
07:13 Ravi Patel: i'll paste a sample json after the call — it includes user, role, request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency, and action.
07:20 Priya Singh: curious about encryption in transit certs and rotation frequency?
07:24 Ravi Patel: TLS 1.2+ with mTLS options for private. key rotation policy is customer-driven for BYOK; for platform keys we rotate quarterly and keep rotation proofs.
07:36 Maya Chen: what about logging PII in traces? do you scrub payloads in traces?
07:40 Ravi Patel: traces capture metadata not payloads by default; customers can opt-in to additional traces but we scrub or tokenise payloads unless explicitly requested.
07:49 Dana Liu: can we recap action items and next steps?
07:52 Carlos Ortega: sure before that — competitors: we've been looking at openai enterprise and anthro pics and aws sage maker — curious on cost and reliability tradeoffs.
07:59 Dana Liu: noted. ok recap: we'll send SOC2 + ISO, the security brief on KMS/BYOK, sample audit logs, network diagram and onboarding steps, and a pricing sheet for hosted/dedicated/private. we'll also schedule a tech deep-dive with luma's network/security engineers.
08:18 Maya Chen: sounds good. any timelines?
08:21 Dana Liu: i'll get the docs out by end of week; ravi will coordinate the tech call for week of april 5th.
08:28 Priya Singh: i'll coordinate internally and send availability.
08:30 Dana Liu: perfect. thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
